Within the Provo-Orem metro area, Pleasant Grove spreads across 9.18 square miles at about 4,623 feet. The ZIP code is 84062. Battle Creek Canyon rises above town, with the roughly 50 foot Battle Creek Falls inside it, and a large white G is painted on the hillside.

Growth has nearly stalled. The 2020 census found 37,721 residents, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 37,773. Owners live in two out of every three homes.

Use these as a rough backdrop. They cannot price your particular house.

Battle Creek was the original name, taken from an 1849 clash between settlers and a small band of Ute people. A nearby cottonwood grove inspired the later name. Settlement began in 1850 and incorporation came on January 18, 1855. Today it goes by Utah's City of Trees, and Strawberry Days, first held on June 21, 1922, still fills the third week of June with a rodeo, parades and a carnival.

Expect cold winters and hot, dry summers: 16.43 inches of precipitation in an average year, 41.4 inches of snow, and recorded temperatures from 104 degrees down to minus 19.

  • Snow load tests any roof that has been patched or has aging shingles.
  • A tired furnace gives itself away the first cold January.
  • Hot summers put the air conditioner's age on a buyer's radar.

None needs fixing for an as-is cash sale, though a traditional buyer's inspector will likely bring them up.

Public schools currently belong to Alpine School District, which ends on July 1, 2027. After that, Pleasant Grove joins the new Timpanogos district with Orem, Lindon and Vineyard. Town also has John Hancock Charter School, Lincoln Academy and the private, accredited Liahona Preparatory Academy (K-12).

Because names and boundaries are shifting, families should verify the attendance area for any address before relying on it.

The average commute for Pleasant Grove workers is 21.7 minutes. Utah Valley University in Orem and Brigham Young University in Provo are both nearby, so say in your listing how long the drive is to those campuses.

Own a house with a basement apartment or other second unit? Call the Pleasant Grove planning office to learn how the city classifies it. Lenders and title companies will want to know whether the unit is allowed.

  • A family can be one person living alone, or people related by blood, marriage, adoption or guardianship plus up to two unrelated people who pay no rent.
  • A family can also be up to four related or unrelated people living as one housekeeping unit.
  • A tiny home is a subordinate dwelling in a detached accessory structure of at least 192 square feet, on a permanent foundation with all required utilities.

Permit or registration steps for an apartment are set elsewhere in the code, so confirm with the city how yours was approved.

The county assessor values Pleasant Grove homes and the county bills them. A valuation notice lands in late July. To contest the market value, file with the county Board of Equalization by September 15, or by March 31 if you qualify for a late appeal. Tax notices come mid to late October.

With the 45% exemption, a primary residence is taxed on 55% of market value, so long as someone occupies it for at least 183 consecutive days a year. New owners may receive a declaration form from the county assessor. A rental that lacks a full-time eligible occupant is classed as a secondary residence. The Treasurer's number for payoffs on delinquent tax is 801-851-8255.

The deed to a Pleasant Grove property goes on record at the county, in Provo at 100 East Center Street, Suite 1300. Staff accept documents that meet state requirements, but they do not draft or notarize, interpret papers, advise on law or search titles.

Your closing company ordinarily files for you. A free alert service called Property Watch will also email you when anything is recorded against a property you monitor. The recorder's phone number is 801-851-8179.

sections.h2: What to gather before you sell
sections.html:
Some paperwork keeps a sale here on schedule. Dig up the deed or closing statement, the newest valuation notice and tax bill, and approval records for any basement unit. A rented house calls for the lease and a move-out date. An estate house needs whatever transfer papers exist.

Gaps are normal and often fixable through the title company, so a missing paper should not delay your call. The earlier we hear your situation, the sooner you get a straight answer on price and timing.

sections.h2: Selling a house that needs work
sections.html:
Plenty of owners here hold a house that wants a new roof, a furnace or a full cosmetic refresh. Doing that work before a traditional listing eats money and time, and a lender may still ask for more. An as-is sale hands that burden to the buyer. You give up some potential price in return for speed and certainty, and only you can say whether that fits.

Snap a few photos and jot down known problems. Honest notes let us price the house accurately the first time.

sections.h2: What happens after you accept an offer
sections.html:
Once you say yes, the title or escrow company opens the file and orders a title search. They confirm who owns the house, whether any liens or unpaid property tax sit against it, and what the payoff will be. Pleasant Grove's tax bill follows the county calendar, so a balance owed is simply paid from your proceeds at closing. You sign, the deed is recorded, and you collect the money. There is no appraisal to wait on and no buyer's loan that can fall through at the last minute, which is the usual reason a conventional closing slips.

Sellers who need a particular date, for a move or a probate deadline, can ask for it up front. Closing is set with you, not around a lender's calendar.

sections.h2: Selling a Pleasant Grove house for cash
sections.html:
The people who call us own an inherited house, a home that needs big repairs, a basement apartment with murky paperwork, or face a move that cannot wait on a listing.

  1. Describe the property to us.
  2. We look it over and quote a price reflecting its condition.
  3. Once you agree, an escrow or title company arranges closing.
  4. The deed is filed with the county and you receive payment.

No repairs, no cleaning, since we buy as-is.

faqs.q: What is the population of Pleasant Grove, Utah?
faqs.a: About 37,726 people lived here at the 2020 census. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 37,773.

faqs.q: Which school district will Pleasant Grove homes belong to after 2027?
faqs.a: Timpanogos, a new district, replaces Alpine School District on July 1, 2027, and Pleasant Grove is assigned to it. Verify with the boundary map.

faqs.q: When must a Pleasant Grove property tax appeal be filed?
faqs.a: File with the Utah County Board of Equalization by September 15, online, by email, by mail or in person.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Pleasant Grove house with an unapproved basement apartment?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy as-is, so the apartment's status need not be settled first, though it is smart to ask the city how it was approved.

faqs.q: Do I need to repair my house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. Because we buy as-is, roofs, furnaces and cosmetic work stay off your to-do list.
